name: Medications and Home Pharmacy for Ornamental Fish
description: The most common medications and supplies for aquarium fish, mapped to the diseases in diseases-freshwater.json and diseases-saltwater.json.
homePharmacyScale: Home pharmacy rating: 1 = unimportant, 10 = very important. Separately for freshwater and marine; null = not relevant for this water type.
homePharmacyCriteria: Is fast action required (no time to obtain it)?
Freely available and safe for use by laypeople?
legalNotes: Legal situation in Germany. Ornamental fish medicines without prescription-only substances are exempt from marketing authorisation under § 4 TAMG and freely available.
Antimicrobial veterinary medicines (antibiotics, metronidazole) are prescription-only under Art. 34 Regulation (EU) 2019/6.
The status may differ in other countries.
legalStatusVerifiedNote: legalStatusVerified = true: status confirmed in the EU product database, by law or by the manufacturer; false: plausible but not individually checked.
disclaimer: No dosage information – always follow the package insert or veterinary instructions. Product examples are not a recommendation of a particular brand.

legalStatusLabels.not_a_medicine: not a medicine – freely available (shops, pharmacy, drugstore)

medications.name: Malachite green + formaldehyde (combination product)
medications.legalNote: Ornamental fish medicines without prescription-only substances are exempt from marketing authorisation under § 4 TAMG and freely available.

indications.disease: Skin and Gill Clouding by Protozoa (Costia, Chilodonella, Trichodina)

cautions: Not for cartilaginous fish (e.g. rays) and invertebrates (according to the package leaflet).
Loaches, catfish and knifefish are considered very sensitive to malachite green.
Formaldehyde lowers oxygen levels – aerate strongly.
Malachite green is light-sensitive – store in the dark.
medications.use: Dosage and duration strictly according to the package insert; remove activated carbon during treatment and use it afterwards to remove residues.

homePharmacy.reason: Covers the most common aquarium disease (white spot) and other skin parasites, freely available, fast action is crucial.

medications.name: Malachite green + methylene blue + ethacridine (combination product)
medications.legalNote: Ornamental fish medicines without prescription-only substances are exempt from marketing authorisation under § 4 TAMG and freely available.

indications.disease: Skin and Gill Clouding by Protozoa (Costia, Chilodonella, Trichodina)

cautions: Stains silicone, decoration and water.
Scaleless species react sensitively.
Do not combine with other remedies.
medications.use: Dosage and duration strictly according to the package insert; remove activated carbon during treatment and use it afterwards to remove residues.

homePharmacy.reason: Equivalent alternative to the malachite green/formaldehyde product; one of the two is enough in the home pharmacy.

medications.name: Copper sulfate + acriflavine + ethacridine + methylene blue (combination product)
medications.legalNote: Ornamental fish medicines without prescription-only substances are exempt from marketing authorisation under § 4 TAMG and freely available.

indications.disease: Fin Rot and Bacterial Ulcers (Aeromonas, Pseudomonas)

cautions: Contains copper – considerably more toxic in soft water with low KH (UF/IFAS FA008).
Lethal to invertebrates.
medications.use: Dosage and duration strictly according to the package insert; remove activated carbon during treatment and use it afterwards to remove residues.

homePharmacy.reason: Helps with fungal infection and as wound protection; fungal infection is usually secondary, hence medium priority.

medications.name: Copper product for marine aquariums (copper therapy)
activeSubstances: copper (Cu²⁺, e.g. as sulfate or citrate)
medications.legalNote: Available in specialist shops as an ornamental fish remedy or water additive; check the legal status of the specific product.
cautions: Therapeutic range 0.15–0.20 mg/L free copper; check daily with a copper test (UF/IFAS FA165).
Only in a quarantine tank without invertebrates, calcareous rock and sand.
Dwarf angelfish and some other species are copper-sensitive.
Return invertebrates only at no more than 0.01 mg/L copper.
medications.use: Dose only with a copper test; keep the concentration in the therapeutic range for the entire treatment.

homePharmacy.reason: Standard therapy against the two most dangerous marine parasites – but only useful together with a copper test and quarantine tank.

medications.name: Praziquantel
medications.legalNote: Freely available in the pet trade (manufacturer: water treatment for ornamental fish).

indications.disease: Skin and Gill Flukes (Monogenea: Gyrodactylus, Dactylogyrus)
Skin and Gill Flukes in Marine Fish (Monogenea)

cautions: Check tolerance for invertebrates with the manufacturer.
Repeat treatment for egg-laying gill flukes.
medications.use: Dosage and duration strictly according to the package insert; remove activated carbon during treatment and use it afterwards to remove residues.

homePharmacy.reason: Skin and gill flukes are common, especially in new fish; well tolerated and freely available.

medications.name: Emamectin (nematodes)
medications.legalNote: According to the manufacturer, the first freely available ornamental fish remedy against nematodes; other substances (levamisole, fenbendazole) are prescription-only.
cautions: Shrimp and crayfish do not tolerate the treatment (manufacturer).
medications.use: Dosage and duration strictly according to the package insert; remove activated carbon during treatment and use it afterwards to remove residues.

homePharmacy.reason: Camallanus is common in livebearers; the only freely available remedy against roundworms.

medications.name: Emamectin benzoate + denatonium benzoate (parasitic crustaceans)
medications.legalNote: According to the manufacturer freely available; previous remedies against parasitic crustaceans were prescription-only or toxic.
cautions: Snails, mussels, crayfish and insect larvae do not tolerate the treatment.
Sturgeons react sensitively.
Repeat treatment after about 3 weeks.
medications.use: Dosage and duration strictly according to the package insert; remove activated carbon during treatment and use it afterwards to remove residues.

homePharmacy.reason: Rarely needed in aquariums, but important for garden ponds.

medications.name: Diflubenzuron (parasitic crustaceans, pond)
medications.legalNote: Sold as a medicine for ornamental fish in garden ponds; exemption status not checked in the EU database.
cautions: Moulting inhibitor – kills all crustaceans.
Switch off UV clarifiers during treatment (manufacturer).
medications.use: Dosage and duration strictly according to the package insert; remove activated carbon during treatment and use it afterwards to remove residues.

homePharmacy.reason: Pond product; hardly needed in aquariums.

medications.name: Sodium chloride (pure salt)
medications.legalStatusLabel: not a medicine – freely available (shops, pharmacy, drugstore)
medications.legalNote: Not a medicine; use salt without iodine and without anti-caking agents.

indications.disease: Skin and Gill Clouding by Protozoa (Costia, Chilodonella, Trichodina)
Skin and Gill Flukes (Monogenea: Gyrodactylus, Dactylogyrus)

cautions: Not all fish species and plants tolerate salt.
For nitrite: 10 mg/L chloride per 1 mg/L nitrite (UF/IFAS FA16).
medications.use: As a prolonged or short bath; adjust the concentration to the fish species.

homePharmacy.reason: Cheap, long shelf life, versatile – first aid for nitrite poisoning and supportive for skin parasites.

medications.name: Potassium permanganate
medications.legalStatusLabel: not a medicine – freely available (shops, pharmacy, drugstore)
medications.legalNote: Chemical, not an approved ornamental fish medicine.

indications.disease: Skin and Gill Clouding by Protozoa (Costia, Chilodonella, Trichodina)
Skin and Gill Flukes (Monogenea: Gyrodactylus, Dactylogyrus)

cautions: Strong oxidiser – gill damage on overdose.
Organic load consumes the active substance; the required amount varies greatly.
Wear gloves and safety glasses.
medications.use: Only with experience or expert guidance.

homePharmacy.reason: Effective but hard to dose and risky – unsuitable for the home pharmacy.

medications.name: Clove oil (eugenol)
medications.legalStatusLabel: not a medicine – freely available (shops, pharmacy, drugstore)
medications.legalNote: Not a veterinary medicine; available in pharmacies and drugstores. Killing vertebrates requires a reasonable cause and expertise – if in doubt, ask a veterinarian.
cautions: According to the AVMA guidelines 'acceptable with conditions' for fish – use a product with a known eugenol content and ensure death with a second method.
Dissolve in alcohol first, as clove oil is poorly soluble in water.
medications.use: For incurably ill animals (e.g. neon tetra disease, fish tuberculosis, DGIV).

homePharmacy.reason: Several diseases are incurable; quick, humane euthanasia prevents suffering and stops infection.

supplies.name: Water test kits (ammonium, nitrite, nitrate, pH, GH, KH)
supplies.legalStatusLabel: not a medicine – freely available (shops, pharmacy, drugstore)
cautions: Drop tests are usually more accurate than test strips; observe the expiry date.
supplies.use: Measure first whenever disease is suspected; use the values for the measurable questions in the diagnosis tree.

homePharmacy.reason: Basis of every diagnosis – many diseases start with poor water.

supplies.name: Copper test kit
supplies.legalStatusLabel: not a medicine – freely available (shops, pharmacy, drugstore)

indications.disease: Poisoning by Copper and Fish Medication (Invertebrates)
Poisoning by Copper and Fish Medication (Marine Invertebrates)

supplies.use: Mandatory with any copper therapy; check before returning invertebrates.

homePharmacy.reason: Prerequisite for copper therapy in marine tanks; for monitoring in invertebrate tanks.

supplies.name: Activated carbon (washed, granular)
supplies.legalStatusLabel: not a medicine – freely available (shops, pharmacy, drugstore)

indications.disease: Poisoning by Copper and Fish Medication (Invertebrates)
Poisoning by Copper and Fish Medication (Marine Invertebrates)

cautions: Remove during medication.
Do not use lignite-based carbon permanently with surgeonfish (HLLE risk).
supplies.use: Remove medication residues after treatment; use immediately in case of poisoning.

homePharmacy.reason: Needed after every treatment and first aid for poisoning.

supplies.name: Quarantine tank (with heater, air pump, sponge filter)
supplies.legalStatusLabel: not a medicine – freely available (shops, pharmacy, drugstore)

indications.disease: Poisoning by Copper and Fish Medication (Invertebrates)

cautions: Run the sponge filter in the main tank so it is cycled in an emergency.
supplies.use: Quarantine new animals for 3–4 weeks; treatments without risk to invertebrates and plants.

homePharmacy.reason: Allows treatment without endangering the main tank; practically indispensable for marine tanks.
